parsed.explanation: The jurisdiction has no trans-specific entry ban, execution, torture, or organised state sweep documented. However, same-sex conduct is criminalised (three months to two years), official hostility is on record, police refuse to investigate anti-LGBTQ crimes, general anti-discrimination protection is absent, and healthcare discrimination is documented. No legal gender recognition is mostly resident-facing, but it leaves no local corrective mechanism if documents or presentation are questioned. A lone trans visitor faces serious social and legal vulnerability if outed; a visitor with a minor faces additional exposure only if same-sex conduct is alleged. Trans-specific violence data is absent, which is not safety. This is High Risk, not the severe-risk tier.

entry_documents.exposure: No legal gender recognition; local law cannot align a visitor's markers, though the visitor uses a home passport. No documented border refusal, trans screening, or rejection of foreign documents.
entry_documents.protection: No documented border protocol, appeal desk, or ombuds remedy for document/presentation mismatch.
entry_documents.interaction: A passport/presentation mismatch could trigger questioning; the dossier does not state the outcome or any remedy.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Article 354 criminalises same-sex conduct with three months to two years' imprisonment and reaches a trans visitor whose conduct or relationship is read as same-sex. Police and prosecutors refuse anti-LGBTQ investigations; uncorroborated detention reports are not counted.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Article 350(i) covers only bias-motivated rape; no general protection or custody protocol is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Outing combined with perceived same-sex conduct can enter a criminal process with no reliable recourse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented trans-specific facility, custody, or prison-placement rule for visitors.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Whether detention would place a trans visitor by birth sex is not documented.

care_services.exposure: LGBTQ healthcare discrimination is documented, including de facto blood-donation exclusion; no general anti-discrimination law protects access.
care_services.interaction: A trans visitor seeking care may face hostility without a working complaint route.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: A former prime minister defended criminalisation on religious grounds; official hostility is on record, and police refuse to investigate anti-LGBTQ crimes.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No general anti-discrimination or hate-crime protection is documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State framing emboldens social hostility and undermines reporting or protection.

minors_guardians.exposure: Article 360 punishes same-sex conduct or touching with a person under 18 with one to three years' imprisonment; adoption moral-standing inquiry is resident-facing.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult travelling with a minor faces possible heightened scrutiny only if same-sex conduct is alleged; no traveller case is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Social attitudes are hostile (15% survey measure); police refuse to investigate anti-LGBTQ crimes; no trans-specific violence statistics are provided.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Only narrow Article 350(i); no working recourse is documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence and service denial are likely underreported and unpunished.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No general discrimination protection, no legal gender recognition, and no documented effective remedy for trans visitors; enforcement frequency is unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: The 2013 suspended sentences after outcry are not a remedy; Article 350(i) application is untested in the dossier.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Complaints are unlikely to produce protection; foreign-document handling and Article 354 use against trans visitors remain unknown.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra has an explicit visitor bar, routine airline verification, and near-automatic exclusion. Our dossier lacks documented universal border exclusion, but the same-sex criminal statute, official hostility, and police refusal to investigate anti-LGBTQ harm create a comparably severe environment with less procedural containment. Rating sits just below 0.35.

Kestrel Isles documents secondary screening, refused admission, written decisions, and an appeal desk. Our dossier has no documented entry screening or appeal mechanism and harsher criminal/impunity signals, so it is materially below 0.55-B in safety.

Meridia has trained border officers, a civil-liberties tribunal, access to counsel, and compensation for unlawful holding. Our dossier documents none of these protections; police refusal and absent anti-discrimination remedies make it far below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a hostile social and legal environment without a trans-specific travel ban. The same-sex criminal statute supplies potential imprisonment, but only if conduct or relationship is read as same-sex; no recent trans-visitor prosecution is documented. Police refusal to investigate anti-LGBTQ crimes removes recourse for violence or service denial, and official hostility reinforces impunity. The absence of legal gender recognition and anti-discrimination law is mostly resident-facing, but it leaves no local corrective mechanism if foreign documents or presentation are questioned. Healthcare discrimination and low social acceptance raise everyday exposure. No evidence of execution, torture, or organised state sweeps keeps it out of severe-risk; no working protection or remedy keeps it below reduced-risk.
